topic_gates.evidence: The rust-cardigan woman at picture-left offers a heart-panel robot into the seated man's right palm while looking at his face. The sage-shirt woman at picture-right leans toward that same man, holds his upper arm/sleeve and looks at his face. Both vectors share the same visible target.

Left interest combines a heart-shaped gift cue, close body orientation, mutual eye contact and a soft personal smile. Right interest combines intimate leaning, affiliative arm contact, absorbed gaze and a soft smile at the same man. These mutually reinforcing cues read as courtship/affection rather than a work group alone; private desire or consent is not asserted.

The man actively supports the left gift and returns its giver's gaze, but his left arm simply rests while the right woman clasps his upper-arm sleeve. A second affectionate approach is visible, yet he neither returns her contact nor directs a distinct visible response toward her. Under the frozen multi-approach recipient criterion, passive contact alone does not establish that he registers or participates in both; the full gate stays failed rather than inferred.

All four faces, the common seated target, left gift-to-palm connection and right woman-to-arm contact are readable together in the same saved frame. The third woman holds two mugs and looks toward the central group, but her romantic/rival status is weaker and is not needed to meet the at-least-two frozen criterion.

authorial_checks.evidence: Tools, robot assemblies, workbenches and a polished articulated robot establish a robotics studio with plausible near-future technology cues. The roof window shows a meteor and twilight skyline. Actual future chronology or robot autonomy cannot be proven from the still.

The picture-left woman has a short dark bob, fine parted fringe, brown eyes, a softly tapered facial impression and rosy lips consistent with the visible portrait cues. Scale and expression differ, so this is appearance resemblance only, not identity or age proof.

Both leading physical contacts are coherent and traceable, but the right woman's hand grasps the man's upper-arm sleeve; her right arm does not pass through his relaxed left elbow as written. Only one gift-giver hand is clearly visible on the robot while the man supports its base; her plural hands supporting the base is not jointly observable. The full intended linked-elbow/handover mechanism therefore does not pass.

overall_reason: Shared romantic target and multiple affectionate vectors are readable, but the recipient's response to more than one approach and the intended linked-elbow/handover mechanism are only partially realized. All criteria do not pass simultaneously.
